svg.text: Roof plan, cut at +8.50 · grid B
horizontal cut through the top ring, looking down on the ribs
Cut at +8.50 (crown, 6.00 above the roof base)
through the top ring: printed layers, cast ring
(crossed hatch), insulation and outer layer; crown
opening 1000.
Ribs of grid B, seen from above: two families of
diagonals from the base ring at the eave to the hips
and the top ring.
Base ring: the 300 solid base at the eave (+2.50 to
No horizontal ribs between the base ring and the top
ring in grid B.
Hips: four ribs from the corners of the eave to the
corners of the top ring.
Roof edge at the eave (outside of the 30 outer
layer). Very faint squares = printed layer joints
(real layers 10, drawn every 200 in height).
Buttresses below the roof: their ends show beyond
the roof edge; the wall under the roof is dashed.
from your sketches
assumed by me, to confirm
Notes
The ribs lie inside the shell, between the printed inner
layers and the outer layer; here they are drawn as if the
outer layer, insulation and cladding were transparent, so
their whole run from the eave to the crown can be seen.
Ribs are drawn on the mid-surface of the shell, 160 wide,
with the same geometry as the roof-grid sheets and
sections.
